newsitem.title: GERMANY: Compaq 1996 European sales rise 12 percent.
newsitem.headline: Compaq 1996 European sales rise 12 percent.

text.p: European sales for Compaq Computer Corp. rose 12 percent in 1996 to $6 billion, powered by a strong fourth quarter and solid gains in portable PC and server computer sales, the U.S.computer maker said Thursday.
European gains were dampened by weaker results in Germany, where revenue rose 7.6 percent to 1.4 billion marks ($832.9 million) as unit sales stalled.
Kurt Dobitsch, head of Compaq's German unit, said he was "satisfied" with results in that country, although he admitted Compaq and other large PC makers saw "stagnating market share" in 1996.
"With growth of only 1 percent, the home market showed a flat and disappointing development curve," he said.
Meanwhile, Compaq said it aimed to revive its German unit in 1997 by introducing a line of low-priced personal computers and focusing on sales to small and mid-sized businesses.
A new series of machines due in the next few months would sell for between $2,000 and $2,500, Kurt Dobitsch, managing director of Compaq Computer GmbH, said at a new conference.

Compaq, the No. 1 maker of personal computers, said unit sales of desktop PCs rose 27 percent across Europe, while portable unit sales increased 36 percent and 32 percent for servers, or computers that run networks.
In the fourth quarter, revenue for Europe, the Middle East and Africa rose 44 percent, Compaq said.
